author: blu
body: The IR validator: the one idea worth taking from nanopass. Every rewriting pass is a chance to produce IR that is still well-typed enough to walk and still wrong -- a name left dangling by a substitution, a type dropped on a rebuilt node, a match rewritten down to no branches. None of those crash the pass that made them. They crash, or worse do not crash, three stages later in the emitter, and the search starts in the wrong place. `ir-check` walks a chapter and answers with the list of things wrong with it, so that a malformed chapter is attributed to the pass that produced it.

author: blu
body: It is a checker in a rewriter's clothing. The pipeline's interface is `IRChapter -> IRChapter` and the registry dispatches on a name, so the cheapest way to make the validator placeable anywhere in the pipeline -- `passes=fold-constants,ir-check,inline-leaf-calls,ir-check` -- is to register it as a pass that returns its input unchanged and reports out of band. The violations ride back to the caller in the pass result and become CDX9004 errors in the frontend's bag.

author: blu
body: It halts rather than warns. A warning that the IR is malformed is a warning that the binary about to be written is not the program that was written down; there is nothing to do with that but stop. The bag already carries this meaning -- `compile-to-cdx-with-exit-mode` emits no binary when the frontend bag has errors -- so a violation lands in the bag and the existing halt does the rest. No new halt machinery.

author: blu
body: This paragraph used to add "codegen already refuses it, but by then the pass that dropped the type is long gone." Codegen does not refuse it and never did. There was a code for that refusal -- CDX2041, ErrorTypeInIR, registered in the codegen phase -- and nothing ever raised it; codegen instead PRODUCES `ErrorTy` (`prefer-type-binding` answers it for a name it cannot bind) and renders it as "Unknown". The code is deleted rather than left standing as a refusal nobody performs. It could not honestly be wired anyway while the three holes below exist, because codegen would refuse the valid programs that carry them. This check, here, is the only thing that reports an `ErrorTy` in the IR at all.

author: blu
body: A branch's pattern binds for that branch's guard and body only. The pattern is walked for its binders and for nothing else -- see the Patterns section for why its types are not checked.
